title: VidLaDA: Bidirectional Diffusion Large Language Models for Efficient Video Understanding
claim: Encoding video into spatiotemporal tokens and feeding them with text to a bidirectional diffusion model enables parallel response prediction.
layout: Bottom-to-top flow: video encoder row, then token blocks, then model, then output
description: A tall architecture diagram read from the bottom left, upward and then across. The bottom row starts with stacked input video frames (a photo of a man on a street), then arrows to an orange Vision Encoder trapezoid, a grid of raw frame features, a gray Projector block, a 2x2 spatial pooling grid with inward arrows, and a row of green tokens labeled Spatiotemporal Unrolling. A large hollow arrow carries the tokens up into a dashed blue box. That box shows green visual tokens, cyan text prompt tokens ("What is he doing?"), and yellow noised response tokens with gray [MASK] tokens. Green and cyan bracket arrows below mark full bidirectional connections between visual tokens and the prompt. Black arrows go up into a wide pink Diffusion Language Model bar. Above it, a second dashed box shows the parallel prediction R0, with red arrows marking the tokens filled in from masks ("walking", "singing"). Flame icons mark trainable modules.
caption: The overall architecture of VidLaDA. Input video frames V are encoded and spatially pooled (via 2 × 2 downsampling) before being unrolled into a sequence of Spatiotemporal Visual Tokens EV. These tokens, combined with the text prompt P and the noised response Rt, are processed by the Diffusion Language Model. Unlike autoregressive models, VidLaDA utilizes full bidirectional attention. This design enables global, unconstrained interactions both within and across visual and textual modalities, ultimately facilitating the parallel prediction of the target response R0.
abstract: Current Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) typically encode frames via a vision encoder and employ an autoregressive (AR) LLM for understanding and generation. However, this AR paradigm inevitably faces a dual efficiency bottleneck: strictly unidirectional attention compromises understanding efficiency by hindering global spatiotemporal aggregation, while serial decoding restricts generation efficiency. To address this, we propose VidLaDA, a Video LLM based on Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) that leverages bidirectional attention to unlock comprehensive spatiotemporal modeling and decode tokens in parallel. To further mitigate the computational overhead of diffusion decoding, we introduce MARS-Cache, an acceleration strategy that prunes redundancy by combining asynchronous visual cache refreshing with frame-wise chunk attention. Experiments show VidLaDA rivals state-of-the-art AR baselines (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL and LLaVA-Video) and outperforms DLM baselines, with MARS-Cache delivering over 12x speedup without compromising accuracy. Code and checkpoints are open-sourced at https://github.com/ziHoHe/VidLaDA.
